question: If acot θ = b, then what will be the value of frac{{bcos theta - asin theta }}{{bcos theta + asin theta }}?
solution:
**Given:**

a cot θ = b

**Concept Used:**

cot θ = 1/tan θ 

sin θ/cos θ = tan θ 

**Calculation:**

a cot θ = b

tan θ = a/b

frac{{bcos θ - asin θ }}{{bcos θ + asin θ }} 

Divide by cos θ in numerator and denominator, we get

⇒ ({frac{bcos θ )/(cosθ)- (asin θ)/(cosθ) }}{{(bcos θ)/(cosθ) + (asin θ)/(cosθ) }}

⇒ frac{{b - atan θ }}{{b + atan θ }}

⇒ ({b - atimes frac{a)/(b) }}{{b + atimes (a)/(b) }}

⇒ ({frac{b² - a²)/(b) }}{{(b² + a²)/(b)}}

⇒ (b²-a²)/(b²+a²)

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**
